beats.label: S1 · Cloverton
beats.text: Cliff, Rita, Larry, and Jane — each broken by an accident — hide at Dr. Caulder's manor; a rare trip into town draws Mr. Nobody, who devours Cloverton and abducts Caulder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the team, their reclusion, and the antagonist whose kidnapping drives the whole season.

beats.label: S1 · Vic joins the hunt
beats.text: Cyborg Vic Stone joins the search; the team enters a donkey-portal to save Cloverton, then hunts Caulder while Mr. Nobody torments each of them in turn.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Adds Vic as a permanent member and frames Mr. Nobody as a personal antagonist rather than a plot obstacle.

beats.label: S1 · Jane's Underground
beats.text: Jane descends into her Underground of 64 alters and finally destroys the puzzle-monster of her abusive father, but her alters remain restive and question her authority.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Jane's status as Primary as fragile — the mechanism the next season's coup will exploit.

beats.label: S1 · Silas's lie
beats.text: The Bureau of Normalcy captures Vic; Silas rescues him but Vic learns his father erased his memories — Vic's mother also survived the accident, and Silas chose to save only Vic.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The core wound that defines Vic's ongoing struggle with his cybernetics and identity.

beats.label: S1 · White Space truth
beats.text: Flex Mentallo transports them to the White Space, where Mr. Nobody reveals Caulder engineered every accident that gave them their powers, in his hunt for his own immortality.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The betrayal that recolors the team's relationship with Caulder from here on.

beats.label: S1 · Trapping Mr. Nobody
beats.text: The team disbands but returns when Mr. Nobody kidnaps Danny the Street; Larry nukes them all from inside a giant Ezekiel, trapping Mr. Nobody in a painting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Mr. Nobody as an active threat and reforms the team, however grudgingly, under Caulder's roof.

beats.label: S1 · Dorothy revealed
beats.text: Caulder's secret daughter Dorothy Spinner steps out of Ezekiel's belly; the team survives but has been shrunk to a tiny size, unable to reverse it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the person Caulder built his entire hidden life around — the next season's engine.

cliffhanger.text: The team is tiny at Doom Manor, forced to reckon with the fact that Caulder — their savior — deliberately ruined their lives to gain immortality, and that his hidden teenage daughter Dorothy carries some power he was desperate to protect the world from.
questions: Why was Caulder so terrified of what Dorothy might do that he built a manor to hide her?
Can the team ever forgive Caulder for orchestrating the accidents that broke them?
With Mr. Nobody trapped and Caulder exposed, who or what is the team actually working against now?

characters.name: Niles Caulder / The Chief
characters.line: The team's mentor and secret architect of their accidents, a Victorian-era immortal desperately trying to extend his life to protect his daughter Dorothy.

characters.name: Cliff Steele / Robotman
characters.line: A former NASCAR driver whose brain lives in a robotic body; obsessed with reconnecting with his adult daughter Clara, who thinks he's dead.

characters.name: Rita Farr
characters.line: A 1950s actress who becomes a shapeless blob under stress; long since lost any sense of who she is.

characters.name: Larry Trainor / Negative Man
characters.line: Bandaged ex-Air Force pilot sharing his body with a Negative Spirit that increasingly acts on its own; estranged from his wife and lover John Bowers.

characters.name: Jane / Crazy Jane
characters.line: Primary alter of a woman with 64 super-powered personas born from her father's abuse; her core alter is a mute child named Kay.

characters.name: Victor Stone / Cyborg
characters.line: Detroit's half-machine superhero, joined the team after learning his father Silas erased memories of the accident that killed his mother.

characters.name: Dorothy Spinner
characters.line: Caulder's teenage daughter with an ape-like face, immortal through her mother Slava; can materialize creatures from her imagination.

characters.name: Mr. Nobody / Eric Morden
characters.line: The team's sardonic narrator and tormentor, a Nazi-era metahuman experiment; trapped inside a painting by season's end.

characters.name: Danny the Street
characters.line: Sentient, genderqueer teleporting street the team befriended, reduced to a lifeless brick after Larry's blast.

beats.label: S2 · A dying Chief
beats.text: Kipling restores the team to full size for Caulder's immortality talisman; Caulder is now dying, and reveals he built Doom Manor to contain his hidden daughter Dorothy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the whole team as a de-facto prison guard for Dorothy, and starts the clock on Caulder's death.

beats.label: S2 · The Candlemaker calls
beats.text: A demonic voice — the Candlemaker — whispers to Dorothy, granting devastating wishes; Caulder's real mission has always been protecting the world from what she could unleash.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's antagonist and explains why Caulder's paranoia was justified.

beats.label: S2 · Personal lives
beats.text: The team drifts into personal lives — Larry reconciles with his son Paul, Cliff visits pregnant daughter Clara, and Rita joins the Cloverton theater with growing acclaim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the family threads each of them will still be tugging on next season.

beats.label: S2 · Roni turns violent
beats.text: Vic dates ex-soldier Roni, then finds she was enhanced by the Ant Farm and dying of it; she steals sex-demon 'Uma Jelly' to re-enhance and commits a revenge murder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the impossible choice Vic will make about Roni at the start of the next season.

beats.label: S2 · Baby Doll and Katy die
beats.text: Dorothy accidentally kills Jane's child alter Baby Doll, then invites the Candlemaker into the Underground to slay Katy; Miranda returns as Primary, deposing Jane.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The coup that removes Jane from her own body and gives the Candlemaker a foothold in her mind.

beats.label: S2 · Miranda is Daddy
beats.text: Kay realizes that Miranda is not Miranda at all but 'Daddy from the Well' — the abusive father manifestation risen from the Underground and now inhabiting Jane's body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal that the thing Jane fears most has taken over her — the exact situation she'll wake up in next season.

beats.label: S2 · Waxed and alone
beats.text: The Candlemaker manifests fully, waxing over Cliff, Rita, Vic, and Larry; Slava appears and tells Dorothy she must face the demon alone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Leaves the team incapacitated with Dorothy as the only one who can end the crisis — the exact frozen moment next season resumes from.

cliffhanger.text: The Doom Patrol lies waxed over, Caulder is aged near death, Daddy-as-Miranda has hijacked Jane's body, and Dorothy stands alone in the yard against the Candlemaker as her long-absent mother Slava watches.
questions: Can Dorothy actually defeat the Candlemaker, or is her only option to give in to him?
Will anything survive of Caulder, and will the team make it out of the wax at all?
Can Jane ever get her body back from Daddy, or is Kay stranded in the Underground for good?

characters.name: Niles Caulder / The Chief
characters.line: Dying without his talisman, tired and terrified for Dorothy; the team keeps him alive out of duty, not affection.

characters.name: Cliff Steele / Robotman
characters.line: Chasing a real relationship with pregnant daughter Clara, whom he's only recently allowed himself to approach.

characters.name: Rita Farr
characters.line: Finally learning to steer her blob-powers and stepping into local theater with real ambition.

characters.name: Larry Trainor / Negative Man
characters.line: Reconciling with son Paul and grandson Dex — an effort that ends with Paul betraying him to the Bureau and Dex shot in the crossfire.

characters.name: Jane
characters.line: Deposed as Primary and trapped in the Underground while 'Miranda' — actually Daddy from the Well — walks her body.

characters.name: Victor Stone / Cyborg
characters.line: Torn between his cybernetics and humanity; dating Roni Evers, whom he now knows is a wanted murderer.

characters.name: Dorothy Spinner
characters.line: Caulder's daughter, immortal from her mother Slava; the Candlemaker calls to her endlessly, wanting to be summoned.

characters.name: The Candlemaker
characters.line: Demonic wish-granting entity bound to Dorothy; has begun manifesting in the real world and can wax victims solid.

characters.name: Willoughby Kipling
characters.line: Occult detective and Knights Templar operative who now holds Caulder's immortality talisman and drops in only when the world is ending.

beats.label: S3 · After the Candlemaker
beats.text: Dorothy befriends the Candlemaker instead of fighting him; the team is unwaxed, but Caulder dies of old age, and Larry finally releases the Negative Spirit and leaves for space.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets the whole board: the antagonist is neutralized, the mentor is gone, and the team's oldest bond is severed.

beats.label: S3 · Death's Night Nurse
beats.text: Death's Night Nurse kills the team; Larry returns with the Dead Boy Detectives to rescue their souls, and Caulder's severed head sacrifices his mind to un-zombify them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Uses up the last of Caulder for good and marks the team's shift from student-heroes to people out of options.

beats.label: S3 · Madame Rouge arrives
beats.text: An amnesiac time-traveler, Laura De Mille, arrives at Doom Manor seeking Caulder; she can shapeshift, and a film reel ties her past directly to Rita and the Bureau.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the person who will become a full team member and Rita's mirror by season's end.

beats.label: S3 · Failing bodies
beats.text: The team faces mortality — Larry births a glowing blue larva he names Keeg, Vic sheds his cybernetics for synthetic skin, Cliff develops Parkinson's, and Jane's alters begin to vanish.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Every character's physical status flips this season; each of these threads is a load-bearing setup for the next.

beats.label: S3 · Sisterhood of Dada
beats.text: The Sisterhood of Dada emerges — escaped Bureau metahumans that Laura once hunted; Rita finds herself unexpectedly drawn to one of their members, Malcolm.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames Laura's guilt and gives Rita the love that will define both her season and her ending.

beats.label: S3 · Rita in 1917
beats.text: Rita time-travels to 1917, joins the Sisterhood, and falls for Malcolm; she loops back to ensure her past self dies at Codsville, recovering her lost memories in the process.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event that makes Rita whole and the reason she can lead the team going forward.

beats.label: S3 · Doom Force forms
beats.text: Laura is exposed as Madame Rouge of the Brotherhood of Evil; when the Brain betrays her, she joins the team to destroy him. Rita rallies them as 'Doom Force,' Laura reluctantly included.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The team stops being a group of shut-ins and starts being an actual super-team — with Laura in it — which is the whole starting position of next season.

cliffhanger.text: Rita has forged the group into a mortal, imperfect superhero unit called Doom Force with Madame Rouge folded in; they aim time-travel and heroism at their future, though nothing in their bodies works right anymore.
questions: Can this fragile band actually function as heroes, or is 'Doom Force' just Rita's wish-fulfillment?
Will Laura truly leave the Brotherhood behind, or is her past still pulling at her?
Can Jane get her alters back, and can Cliff outrun the Parkinson's now living inside his robot body?

characters.name: Rita Farr
characters.line: Newly assertive after recovering her 1917 memories; the closest thing this team has to a leader now.

characters.name: Cliff Steele / Robotman
characters.line: Chasing a real relationship with daughter Clara and grandson Rory; his Parkinson's has begun to intrude on his robot body.

characters.name: Larry Trainor / Negative Man
characters.line: Released the Negative Spirit and returned from space, now hosting a strange glowing larva named Keeg.

characters.name: Jane
characters.line: Her alters have mostly vanished, leaving her and Kay alone in an emptied Underground.

characters.name: Victor Stone
characters.line: Traded his Cyborg cybernetics for synthetic human skin; struggling to be just a man.

characters.name: Laura De Mille / Madame Rouge
characters.line: Shapeshifting time-traveler and former Brotherhood of Evil agent, working her way — awkwardly — into the team's trust.

characters.name: Willoughby Kipling
characters.line: Occult detective and Knights Templar operative who keeps turning up when reality breaks; delivered the un-zombifying head of Caulder.

beats.label: S4 · A ruined 2042
beats.text: Vic and Silas restore Cliff's robot body; a time-trip drops the team in 2042, where zombie Were-butts have devastated Cloverton and killed everyone but a future Vic.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The dark future the entire season is trying to prevent; sets the stakes and the villain type in one beat.

beats.label: S4 · The Were-butt war
beats.text: Cliff mercy-kills a zombified Darren Jones; unbeknownst to the team, other Were-butts led by Teddy and aided by Dr. Yu are quietly preparing war on humanity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Hides the actual monster army in plain sight while the team thinks they've already contained the threat.

beats.label: S4 · Immortus summoned
beats.text: Dr. Janus and Mister 104 begin draining the team's longevity — which Caulder's experiments long ago gave them — to summon Immortus, an ancient reality-destroying deity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's true engine and ties it back to Caulder's original crime against the team.

beats.label: S4 · Losing everything
beats.text: The team loses their longevity to Immortus's agents; Rita and Laura reconcile at last, Vic reacquires his Cyborg cybernetics, and Larry gives his up so Keeg can survive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Each character makes their final identity choice this season, and this beat is where those choices land.

beats.label: S4 · Immortus is Isabel
beats.text: Immortus is finally summoned — but manifests as Rita's amateurish theater rival Isabel Feathers, an unstable diva who rewrites time to make Cloverton adore her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's boss reveal, and the punchline the last stretch of episodes runs on.

beats.label: S4 · Kaleidoscope
beats.text: Isabel scatters the team through time portals to reclaim their longevity; Caulder helps Jane name her trauma, and her alters reunify into a combined persona called Kaleidoscope.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves Jane's series-long arc and gives the team the unified force they need for the final confrontation.

beats.label: S4 · Endings
beats.text: The team defeats Isabel and disbands: Rita dies reunited with Malcolm, Larry burns out with Rama in space, Jane joins Casey in space, Laura burns down the Ant Farm, and Cliff dies at peace with Rory.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final resting state of every character — the actual ending of the show.

cliffhanger.text: The Doom Patrol is dissolved, its members scattered — some dead, some in exile, some in the afterlife. The world moves on without them, and each of them has, at last, chosen how their story ends.
questions: What life does Rory Steele grow into, carrying Immortus's echo of his grandfather's path?
Where does Laura's vengeance end once the Ant Farm is ash?
What do Kaleidoscope-Jane and Casey Brinke actually build for themselves out among the stars?

characters.name: Cliff Steele / Robotman
characters.line: Fully restored robot body, failing brain; ends the show having reconciled with Clara and dying at peace after seeing Rory's future.

characters.name: Rita Farr
characters.line: The team's undisputed leader through the whole crisis; dies of old age and reunites with Malcolm in the afterlife.

characters.name: Larry Trainor / Negative Man
characters.line: Merged with the alien Keeg; leaves Earth with the reassembled Rama and burns out with him in space.

characters.name: Jane / Kaleidoscope
characters.line: Reunifies with all her alters under a shared persona; leaves Earth for space with Casey Brinke.

characters.name: Victor Stone / Cyborg
characters.line: Reclaimed his Cyborg cybernetics for the final fight; the only member who ends the show back in a hero's costume.

characters.name: Laura De Mille / Madame Rouge
characters.line: Fully accepted by the team; ends the show alone, slaughtering every Ant Farm employee with a flamethrower.

characters.name: Isabel Feathers
characters.line: Rita's amateur-theater rival, made the vessel of Immortus; a needy diva rewriting reality to be loved, defeated when the team refuses her.

characters.name: Casey Brinke
characters.line: Space-adventurer heroine from Dorothy's favorite comic book, made real; leaves Earth with Jane at the end.
